key_insight: Noisy module-to-module links can support fault-tolerant logical operations in modular quantum computers, with much higher interface noise tolerated than within-QPU noise.
engineering_relevance: This suggests modular architectures can scale using imperfect entanglement links while still preserving logical reliability for distributed quantum computation.
method: Circuit-level simulations of fault-tolerant nonlocal CNOT gates using lattice surgery between QPUs
Rotated surface-code encoding with noisy Bell-pair interfaces
Heuristic graph-based ancilla minimization for preparing distributed logical GHZ states
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative logical error-rate simulations showing interfaces can tolerate roughly an order of magnitude more noise than intra-QPU operations with only a minor threshold reduction.
watch_item: The results depend on the assumed noise model and on the practicality of generating and distributing sufficiently high-quality Bell pairs at scale.
paper_title: Fault-Tolerant Logical Operations and Efficient State Preparation in Modular Quantum Architectures with Noisy Interfaces
